name: Apiaka-Tocantins
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.note: Extinct Cariban variety known only from Ehrenreich 1895 and Krause 1936 wordlists per Glottolog; no phonological description exists.

new_statements.quote: Consonantverbindungen sind im Inlaut häufig: tp, mp, pt, tk, kp, pk. Besonders auffallend: tχ, ntχ, ptχ, mtχ. Consonantische Endungen sind: [r?], n, t, ṅ, m. Der Accent liegt in der Regel auf der (meist kurzen) Endsilbe.
new_statements.translation: Consonant clusters are frequent word-internally: tp, mp, pt, tk, kp, pk. Especially striking: tχ, ntχ, ptχ, mtχ. Consonantal endings are: [r?], n, t, ṅ, m. The accent lies as a rule on the (mostly short) final syllable.
new_statements.citation: Ehrenreich, Paul. 1895. Materialien zur Sprachenkunde Brasiliens V: Die Sprache der Apiaka (Para). Zeitschrift für Ethnologie 27: 168-176.
new_statements.locator: p. 171, section 'I. Lautlehre', last sentence (archive.org item zeitschriftfret12urgegoog, leaf n196)
new_statements.check: confirmed by a second reader, with minor differences
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened the held page image (= ZfE 27, 1895, p.171; also p.4 of the assembled 9-page PDF and line 203 of the scanned excerpt). Under the heading 'I. Lautlehre', after the vowel/consonant inventory, the last sentence of the page reads exactly: 'Der Accent liegt in der Regel auf der (meist kurzen) Endsilbe.' -- verbatim as reported. The two preceding sentences also match ('Consonantverbindungen sind im Inlaut haufig: tp, mp, pt, tk, kp, pk. Besonders auffallend: tχ, ntχ, ptχ, mtχ. Consonantische Endungen sind:...'); the only divergence is the list of final consonants, which sits in the damaged gutter margin and on the image looks like 'n, k, ṅ, m' rather than the first reader's '[r?], n, t, ṅ,…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word accent normally falls on the final syllable, which is usually a short vowel; 'in der Regel' (as a rule) implies some items deviate, but no exceptions are listed.
new_statements.exceptions: None named; only the hedge 'in der Regel'. Individual vocabulary items carry Ehrenreich's diacritics but no explicit accent discussion beyond this sentence.
new_statements.domain_note: Impressionistic statement about isolated elicited words (a c. 150-item vocabulary from three speakers at Praia Grande, lower Tocantins, 1888 Araguaya trip); citation forms, no phrase-level data.
new_statements.identity_note: Ehrenreich's 'Apiaka (Para)' is explicitly the Cariban Apiaká of the lower Tocantins (Praia Grande dos Arroios / Arapari, Pará), which he distinguishes at length from the Tupian Apiaká of the Tapajós/Juruena (apia1248); he suggests the group's real name may be 'Apingui'. Matches glottocode apia1247.
